# Senoia Eyecare

Senoia Eyecare is a boutique, doctor-owned optometry practice in Senoia, Georgia. The practice opened in 2024 and is located at 7280 GA-16 Suite F, Senoia, Georgia 30276. It serves Senoia and the surrounding Coweta County communities, including Newnan, Sharpsburg, Tyrone, Peachtree City, and Fayetteville.

The practice positions itself as deliberately small and unhurried — comprehensive exams, careful frame styling, and time for questions. Appointments are booked through an external Eyefinity scheduler at https://www.senoiaeyecare.com/book.

## Doctors

### Dr. Ross Montgomery, OD — Owner & Optometrist

Trained in ocular disease. Most days, that means catching the small things before they turn into big ones. Dr. Montgomery graduated Cum Laude from Valdosta State University with a BS in Biology, then earned his Doctor of Optometry from the PA College of Optometry in 2013. He completed a residency at the Woolfson Eye Institute in Atlanta, working alongside ocular disease specialists. Outside the office he's married to Erica, raising two sons, and spends his time fishing, woodworking, cooking, and anything that gets him outdoors.

### Dr. Taylor Williamson, OD — Optometrist

Kids, families, contact lens fits — including the tricky ones. Dr. Williamson grew up in Bismarck, North Dakota, and graduated from Concordia College in Moorhead in 2015 as a member of the Tri-Beta Biological Honor Society. She earned her Doctor of Optometry from the Southern College of Optometry in Memphis in 2019, then moved to Georgia and has been practicing in the Peach State ever since. She met her husband in optometry school. They share a house with three energetic dogs and a steady rotation of creative projects — model railroading, crochet, writing, and just about anything else she can get her hands on.

## Services

### Comprehensive Eye Exams (https://www.senoiaeyecare.com/eye-exams)

Annual evaluations with advanced retinal imaging. The exam looks at vision, eye health, and conditions a patient cannot see for themselves — glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, dry eye, early macular changes. Typical exam runs about 45 minutes. Pretest includes auto-refraction and retinal imaging; the doctor's portion follows. Patients should bring insurance card, photo ID, current glasses or contacts, and a list of medications. New patient paperwork is emailed before the visit.

### Contact Lens Fitting (https://www.senoiaeyecare.com/contacts)

Soft, toric (for astigmatism), and multifocal contact lenses fit in-chair — not assumed from the glasses prescription. New wearers are welcome and trained on insertion, removal, and care. Every fitting starts with a comprehensive eye exam and ends with a follow-up to verify fit and vision. Reorders are handled through Marlo at https://meetmarlo.com/patient-signin.

### Pediatric & Family Care (https://www.senoiaeyecare.com/pediatric-family)

Gentle exams for children from age three onward, with parents in the room. The practice tracks sight development across the school years and watches for signs that affect learning — focusing problems, eye teaming, refractive shifts. As an InfantSEE provider, Senoia Eyecare offers a no-cost vision assessment for babies between 6 and 12 months. Family appointments can be scheduled in a single quiet morning.

### Frames (https://www.senoiaeyecare.com/frames)

A small, curated wall of frames. Independents from Spain and Chicago beside American icons, plus a featured Maui Jim polarized sunwear collection. Frames are tried on with one-on-one styling — no pressure, no commission-driven nudging. The selection is intentionally edited, not exhaustive.

## Insurance

Most major vision and medical insurance plans are accepted, including:

VSP, EyeMed, Spectera, Superior, Davis, Medicare, Aetna, Blue Cross Blue Shield, Cigna, UMR, UHC, Humana.

Patients are encouraged to verify benefits before their visit. The practice can verify coverage in advance — call (770) 727-6687.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How often should I have an eye exam?**
For most adults, once a year — even if vision feels fine. Annual exams catch quiet changes in eye health (glaucoma, diabetic changes, dry eye) long before they affect how a patient sees, and keep the prescription current.

**What should I bring to my first visit?**
Insurance card, photo ID, current glasses or contact lenses, and a list of any medications. New patient paperwork is emailed ahead so check-in is quick.

**At what age should kids start having eye exams?**
Earlier than most parents expect. As an InfantSEE provider, the practice offers no-cost vision assessments for babies between 6 and 12 months. After that, an exam before kindergarten and yearly through the school years.
